newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MERSON LEAVES ARSENAL AFTER 15 YEARS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MERSON LEAVES ARSENAL AFTER 15 YEARS.

text.p: England midfielder Paul Merson ended 15 years as an Arsenal player on Monday when he joined English first division Middlesbrough in an estimated five million pounds ($8.5 million) move.
Merson, 29, was reported to have signed a five-year contract for relegated Middlesbrough who are expected to lose high profile overseas players Juninho and Fabrizio Ravanelli.
The transfer was a surprise as many had assumed that Merson would end his career at Highbury where it began.
But Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger, who has already spent 14 million pounds ($23.7 million) on new players since the end of last season denied that Merson had been forced out.
"The sale of Merson is not related to any other deal," he said. "You are never happy when you lose a player of Merson's calibre. But it is a good deal for him and a good deal for the club."

Merson enjoyed a roller-coaster career with the London premier league club which peaked with league championship medals in 1989 and 1991 and hit rock bottom in November 1994 when he admitted to cocaine and alcohol addiction.
He was ordered by the English F.A. to spend six months in a rehabilitation clinic but returned to the Arsenal side and played well enough to reclaim a place in the England squad last October.
